title: Crispy Garlic Fish
seoTitle: Mediterranean Baked Cod Tray | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Cod with cherry tomatoes, olives, and capers on one sheet
subtitle: Cod with cherry tomatoes, olives, and capers on one sheet
description: Cod fillets bake with cherry tomatoes, Kalamata olives, capers, garlic, and olive oil until flaky. Designed for hall-scale portioning.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Garlic Fish in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch fish. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat oven and toss vegetables
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 400°F. Toss tomatoes, olives, capers, onion, garlic, oregano, half the olive oil, and salt on two half-sheets until evenly coated.

steps.title: Season fish
steps.instruction: Pat fish dry. Nest fillets among vegetables. Drizzle remaining oil and lemon juice over fish so surfaces look lightly glossed. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Roast until flaky
steps.instruction: Roast 16–20 minutes until fish reads 145°F and flakes with gentle pressure. Tomatoes should burst and release juice into the pan. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Finish with lemon and herbs
steps.instruction: Top with lemon slices and parsley. Fish flesh should look opaque and moist, not chalky or separating into dry strands. Plan about 2 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F until flakes separate. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Portion with pan juices
steps.instruction: Serve each fillet with a spoonful of tomato-olive mixture and pan juices spooned over the top for brightness. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Do not use fish thinner than 1 inch—it overcooks before tomatoes soften.
Add crumbled feta after baking for extra salt and creaminess.
Crusty bread for sopping pan juices keeps crew happy without extra cooking.
tonightSpread: Simple arugula salad with shaved parmesan.
leftovers: Flake fish into a Mediterranean grain salad next day.
Fish tacos with leftover tomato-olive mix as salsa.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Light but satisfying after heavy training days. Minimal dishes and big flavor from pantry staples.
mealPrepNotes: Pit olives if needed. Keep fish cold until it hits the oven. Station: Use parchment on half-sheets for fish release without sticking. Station: Nest fish between tomatoes so fillets stay moist during high-heat roast. Station: Spoon pan juices over portions at the line for extra flavor.
